newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices edge up after APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices edge up after APIs.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices rose slightly on ACCESS, with heating oil leading gains after the American Petroluem Institute (API) reported a decrease in the product's supply last week, traders said.

But trade was unusally thin on a day when API released its weekly U.S. inventory data. Traders said a technical problem, which delayed the start of overnight ACCESS by forty minutes, dampened activity.
"People got a chance to look at (APIs) and see they were at expected levels," a trader said.
U.S. crude oil stocks rose 3.73 million barrels to 289.8 million, close to analyst forecasts of a three million barrel build.
But distillate stocks, which include heating oil, fell by 2.85 million barrels, giving heating oil a more bullish tone.
NYMEX heating oil for February delivery rose 0.47 cents a barrel to 67.30 cents, as around 65 lots traded in the front-month month and 100 moved overall.
Meanwhile, March crude oil was little changed, edging three cents a barrel higher to $23.93 a barrel, as 207 lots traded in the March contract.
Gasoline futures rose about 0.31 cents a gallon to 67.35 cents, as a build in gasoline stocks was offset by refinery maintenance shutdowns.
